title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for short-stay turnover
audience: Owners of short-stay turnover businesses who want repeat bookings and referrals from hosts and property managers they already serve.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the host has confirmed the turnover
instruction.body: Ask for a review or referral after the host has confirmed that the turnover met the checklist, usually after the first few turnovers or at a regular review. Use one sentence, name the next step, and make it easy to say no. One Baylor Keller Center experiment found that a late reminder drew more reviews than an immediate one; that is one experiment. The AMA says the best timing depends on the product, and that experience goods need more time to evaluate. Test the timing with your own hosts.

instruction.heading: Ask every host, and use the review link
instruction.body: Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Ask every host, not only the ones you expect to praise. Filtering who is asked is review gating, which the vendor Podium says Google treats as a violation (not checked against Google's policy). Never write reviews or invent them. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next turnovers in writing
instruction.body: Repeat work in short-stay comes from booking frequency, so offer a standing turnover schedule that follows the host's calendar. Write the scope, the turnover window, the frequency and the price approach, and get the host's confirmation before you change the schedule. The frequency and any seasonal timing are choices to test with your own hosts. A short follow-up after each completed job about a regular plan is one approach that a vendor recommends (Housecall Pro, 8 June 2026). If that follow-up promotes a service by email or text, check the ACMA rules first.

instruction.heading: Check in, and re-contact before busy booking periods
instruction.body: Schedule a short check-in after a set number of turnovers that you test with your own hosts. The research did not find a short-stay benchmark for that number. Before a busy booking period, plan a factual message about the slots you can deliver. Keep it optional, and honour every opt-out within five working days (ACMA).

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next turnover, and write the payment condition, usually that the referred host has booked and completed a paid turnover. Stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across the studies that Xu, Yu and Tu report (2023). Get the referred person's consent before any message goes to them (Clayton Utz, 2017, older source). Host-to-host referral channels were not researched, so treat the scheme as untested.

procedure: After each handover is confirmed, make one review or referral request, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the standing turnover offer with the scope, window, frequency and price approach, and get the host's confirmation.
Schedule the check-in after the number of turnovers you have chosen to test, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan re-contact before each busy booking period you can deliver, and leave out anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books and is paid, apply the reward and record the outcome.
Review each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A turnover cleaner has serviced one host's two apartments for six months. The host says another owner in the building could use the same service, and asks what she would get for the introduction.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner write down before the other owner is contacted, and what should be avoided?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner writes the referral terms first: the reward for the introducer, the payment condition (for example, a paid turnover for the new host), and when the reward is applied. The host passes on the other owner's details, and the cleaner contacts that person only after agreement. The cleaner does not promise a reward that is not in writing, does not offer anything for a review, and does not link any reward to a review's content. If the reward is cash or a credit, the cleaner checks its tax and contract effect with an adviser. The cleaner also accepts only the work that the cleaner's licence and insurance cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the host has confirmed the turnovers meet the checklist.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after the host has confirmed the result.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the host a copy.

commonErrors.error: Filtering which hosts are asked for a review.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask every host and let the review link do the rest.

commonErrors.error: Promising guest ratings or booking results.
commonErrors.prevention: Speak only to the service you deliver.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a host who asked not to hear from you.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and act on each request within five working days.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a host's name, photo, review or property detail needs consent for that use. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, check the OAIC direct-marketing guidance (modified 5 September 2024). Whether the Act applies was not confirmed.

Check-in and re-contact messages by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 2023).
Review platforms and referral schemes have their own rules on incentives. Check each platform's rules, and the ACCC's statement that incentives must be disclosed, before you offer any reward.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. Accept only the work your licence and insurance cover. Licence rules for turnover cleaning were not researched.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the host has confirmed the turnovers, and make it easy to decline.
Offer the standing schedule in writing, before the host's calendar changes.
Set referral terms and payment conditions in writing before anyone refers. Gap: host-to-host referral and repeat rates were not sourced.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a host for a review or referral?
options: Before the first turnover, so the host feels committed
After the host has confirmed the turnover met the checklist
Only after the host has made a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A host wants to post a review with her name and a photo of the unit. What do you need?
options: Her consent for that name and photo
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own view that the photo looks good

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred host books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Written in advance, with the payment condition stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the next turnovers be offered to a host?
options: In writing, with a date and a scope

sourceReferences: Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, published 8 June 2026, updated 9 June 2026. Vendor source; no statistics used. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan; define in the contract how unused visits roll over.

Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: an immediate reminder reduced reviews and a later reminder raised them.

American Marketing Association, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: the right timing depends on the product; experience goods need more time to evaluate.

Google Help, Business Profile review help page, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a review link or QR code may be shared; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; its account of Google's position was not checked against Google's policy. Supports: filtering who is asked for a review is called review gating.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04 per the research file. Supports: consent, accurate sender details, and an unsubscribe honoured within five working days.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across the studies reported. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: a referrer's word alone may not be enough; get the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a service reminder that promotes any service can be a commercial message.

OAIC, 'Direct marketing', https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/organisations/direct-marketing, published 1 May 2019, modified 5 September 2024. Supports: APP 7 governs direct marketing using personal information; opt-out must be simple.

Notes: no source in the research covers host-to-host referral or short-stay repeat rates (gap). The Baylor result is from one experiment. Podium and Housecall Pro are vendor sources. No figures are used from the Xu et al. study.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
